title: Ramadan: the month of the Qur'an
hook: Jibril reviewed the Qur'an with the Prophet ﷺ every Ramadan (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sha'ban, the month of getting ready, and your line was prepare the ground. What did you do early to make something easier? Day five hundred eight.

Ask people what Ramadan is, and most will say: the month Muslims fast. No food or drink from dawn to sunset, for twenty-nine or thirty days. That's true. But open the Qur'an to the verse that sets up the fast, and it introduces the month by something else first. Not hunger. Not the dates at sunset. A book. The fast is there, in the next breath. But the month's name tag, in the Qur'an's own words, is about reading.

Surah Al-Baqarah, verse one hundred eighty-five. Pickthall: "The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind". The verse goes on to say the Qur'an is clear proofs of guidance and the criterion, the furqan we met eleven days ago. Only then does it say: whoever of you is present in the month, let him fast it. So the fast follows the book. Muslims understand that the Qur'an's revelation began in Ramadan, on a night called Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, which we'll reach soon. And there's a scene in Bukhari that makes the month feel like a study partnership. Ibn 'Abbas says the Prophet ﷺ was the most generous of people, and most generous of all in Ramadan, when Jibril met him every night of the month and went over the Qur'an with him. When Jibril met him, Ibn 'Abbas says, he was more generous with good than a wind sent out to bring rain. Another report says Jibril reviewed the whole Qur'an with him once each Ramadan, and twice in the last year of his life. So for many Muslims, Ramadan isn't only about what you don't eat. It's about what you take in. Mosques fill at night for the long tarawih prayers, where the Qur'an is recited in sections. People who rarely open the book during the year try to read it all. The name itself is old. Many lexicographers connect ramad with scorching heat. A hot month, by its name. A month of the book, by its first verse.
screen: `THE MONTH IN WHICH THE QUR'AN CAME.` · `THE FAST FOLLOWS THE BOOK.` · `JIBRIL, EVERY NIGHT OF RAMADAN.` · `MORE GENEROUS THAN THE WIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: take in some of the book. The outline's practice is a juz', one thirtieth of the Qur'an, read in a Ramadan day. For now, start smaller. Sit, and let the breath settle. If you have a Qur'an or an app nearby, read or listen to a few verses, slowly, in Arabic or in translation. If you don't, sit with the verse you just heard, the month in which the Qur'an came. Let it be enough for today. The bell holds the time.
Ramadan. The ninth month, the month of fasting, introduced in the Qur'an first as the month in which the Qur'an was revealed. Today's word.
Your line: the month of the book. Today, swap one scroll for a few lines of something worth reading. Day five hundred eight.

howItsDone: During Ramadan, many Muslims aim to read the whole Qur'an, often one juz' a day, and attend the nightly tarawih prayers, where long portions are recited aloud; the month is also a time of increased charity.

original.note: Arabic: Ramadan, the ninth month; many lexicographers link it to ramad, scorching heat.

trapdoor: what you thought: the month Muslims fast.
what it means: the month the Qur'an first came, introduced that way before the fast is even mentioned.
what a scholar hears: 2:185 names the month; the yearly review (mu'arada) with Jibril is in Bukhari 6 and 4998; ramad (scorching heat) is the usual lexical link for the name.
